themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power Infrastructure
themes.narrative: Nuclear SMR permitting news and 'AI data center power demand crisis' coverage have the market treating power infrastructure as a single overheated trade.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue-confirmed suppliers are still deeply dislocated: BWXT is -27.8% from its 52wH with revenue growing strongly YoY and positive FCF; NXT is -38.7% from high with strong revenue growth, FULL_SIGNAL on the scanner. Both clear all three triple-alignment floors (macro/quality/momentum) and pass the valuation-discipline gate on P/S and P/FCF.
themes.counterRead: Capital has already started separating winners from story stocks: speculative pre-revenue nuclear-adjacent names are being sold hard while the revenue-backed suppliers (BWXT, NXT) sit at a trough. That is the setup, not a reason for caution.
themes.watchFor: BWXT and NXT earnings confirming the revenue-recovery trend continues without margin slippage.

themes.label: Index-Level Calm Masks Magnificent 7 Weakness
themes.narrative: SPY sits only -2.8% from its 52-week high, and low realized volatility reads as 'the market is fine, risk is off the table' at the index level.
themes.dataAnchor: Verified directly (not taken on faith from any single source): the Magnificent 7 (AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/NVDA/META/TSLA) average -20.77% from their own 52-week highs — a 17.97-point gap versus SPY. This isn't a clean, unified move: AAPL is essentially at its own high (-0.6%), while TSLA (-37.2%), MSFT (-31.3%), and META (-25.3%) are doing the heavy lifting on the downside. Cross-checked against the Fed's Senior Loan Officer Survey (SLOOS, FRED series DRTSCILM): net bank tightening of C&I lending standards has fallen from ~45-51% in 2023 to 8.1% as of the most recent (2026-04-01) reading — well below the ~40% level that historically preceded the dot-com, GFC, and 2022 drawdowns.
themes.counterRead: Because SPY is cap-weighted, this concentration means a passive index position is a much more concentrated bet on a handful of mega-cap names than it looks. The historical pattern (leader weakness spreading to the broader index) requires a credit-tightening trigger to actually unwind — and credit is currently loose, not tightening. Read this as index-leadership rotation risk under close watch, not a confirmed rollover: the setup exists, but the trigger (SLOOS crossing back above ~40%) has not fired.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS net tightening (next release) crossing back above ~40% while the Mag7/SPY divergence persists — that combination is the historical pre-drawdown pattern. Also watch whether Mag7 weakness broadens to include AAPL, the one holdout.

themes.label: Enterprise / AI Software SaaS Dislocation
themes.narrative: A year of 'AI will commoditize SaaS' fear has priced enterprise software as if growth is over across the sector.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue math says otherwise for the strongest names, and the valuation-discipline gate (P/S, P/FCF hard caps added 2026-07-24) now confirms which of these are actually cheap versus which are just beaten-down. PLTR was demoted out of triple-aligned status specifically on valuation (P/S 66x, P/FCF 141x) despite strong growth — a name can be dislocated and still expensive.
themes.counterRead: For names that clear both the growth bar and the valuation-discipline floor (not PLTR), the market is pricing a slowdown the numbers don't support. Distinguishing 'cheap and beaten down' from 'expensive and beaten down' is now a mechanical check, not a judgment call.
themes.watchFor: Names newly clearing both quality and valuation floors as prices continue to move.

strategyPosture: Index-level calm (SPY -2.8% from highs) is masking a real, verified divergence: the Magnificent 7 average -20.77% from their own highs, a 17.97-point gap versus SPY. Credit conditions (SLOOS 8.1%, loose) do not currently support calling this a rollover — historically that requires bank tightening back above ~40% — so this reads as leadership rotation under watch, not a confirmed top. SPY, at 47.6% of the portfolio's equity value, is the primary channel of exposure to this risk, not a diversifier from it.
whereWaveBuilds: The next real regime shift is most likely to show up first in the SLOOS quarterly release (next data point after 2026-04-01) — a cross above ~40% net tightening while Mag7/SPY divergence persists would flip this from rotation risk to the historical pre-drawdown pattern (dot-com, GFC, 2022 all shared that combination).
watchFor: SLOOS net tightening (DRTSCILM) crossing back above ~40% — the level that preceded the dot-com, GFC, and 2022 drawdowns
Mag7 weakness broadening to include AAPL, currently the one name still at its own high
HY OAS (credit spreads) widening in tandem with any SLOOS deterioration — confirmation across both market-priced and survey-based credit measures
PLTR-style names (strong growth, failed valuation-discipline check) either re-rating down further or growing into their multiple
BWXT/NXT earnings confirming revenue recovery continues without margin slippage
